annotations.text: The in-game menu: leave, side and settings, opened by Esc or the corner MENU key, with nothing paused and the ship live below. Two candidates are drawn in full: the column carried in from the landing, and the corner panel below it. Whichever wins, side is a list, not a stepper.

The button, as the client already draws it: the key box every pressable thing wears, three bars for the mark, the word MENU beside them on a desktop because that corner is read. Dim until pressed, friend blue while the menu stands.
On a phone the word drops and the mark stands alone in a square of the same box. The column's 320 fits a 390 glass with margin, and RESUME lands where a thumb already lives.

The corner panel, explored: the fight stays live and undimmed beside it. Side is a list because a stepper walks: in a zone with more than two sides, arrows drag you through every team between here and the one you want. A row per side says them all at once, marks yours, and any other is one press; the counts you weigh before switching ride along.

The same panel at a phone's width leaves a strip of live fight showing, the direction's promise kept even here. The strip is also the tradeoff: everything right of the panel is live game under a stray thumb.
The roads not taken, kept for the record: the console center card with settings a page deeper, and the hold-and-flick radial that costs a new grammar.
